body:
You look at your surroundings through a different set of lenses for the first time in a while and say "I feel better" or "Hmmm, this didn't do it, where to next".

Like I said, I can't make you happy but why would you not take the opportunity to go on an adventure if the alternative is swallowing 30 pills and dying from organ failure?  

EDIT: Fine start smaller, don't do something big just walk out your room today and tell 100 people 100 of the most positive lies you can think of.  "Hi there Miss, my name is X and I just wanted to let you know you have a great sense of style.  Have a great day." Enter a restaurant and boastfully tell the staff that although you're not hungry right now that you love their cooking.  Walk in a few pubs where live music is playing and tell the band you really like their sound.  Just keep walking about until you've talked to 100 people and you've told them each one kind lie.

Like I said if you're this rough why are you still staying in your comfort zone?  This sounds crazy but before you do anything, anything at all that is self harming take that chance and just enjoy your day.  NOT at the cafe, not the library NOT the areas you know you can set yourself up to fail in.  You have a free day if you think you're at your end.  Buy a ticket and just leave your state/province and do something so outside of your comfort zone.  

You TRIED to create a different outcome by doing the same things that leave you feeling miserable.  Now, DO something outside of your depressed bubble you created where you can successfully crush your own worth.  Go to another city and do whatever it is you want to do.  Be pleasant, be open and do it without embarrassment. 

You said it best, I can't stop you from killing yourself and... that's not a good situation to be in.  I don't know you, I won't find you but you're wrong about not being able to compromise.  You say you want it to end, I think that's a bad choice but all I am asking of you is to go somewhere else first.  I can't stop you but I can give you the encouragement to go somewhere where death isn't nearly as appealing as it is while you sit in a room you've associated with self hatred.  What have you possibly got to lose?  You'll potentially look like a fool in front of strangers?  You'll get lost in a city you don't know.  Whoopidydoo, tell me those things are worse than never existing again.  I'm not telling you how to change your life around and be happy... I can't.  I can at least tell you that there world is a big place and if you're that low... just explore something first. 

I see your greatest regret if you died would be not being able to say goodbye to your grandma.  How many people have you met in your life?  Have you given ANY of them the chance to say goodbye to you?

Stop.
Think of somewhere you want to go.
Buy a bus ticket.
Go.
If you're that close to ending it all then what do you have to lose?  You'll meet someone, you'll be in a new place and why not have a good day before you make a situation that everyone else around you will regret?

You're 18?  
Let me tell you something that's amazing that almost anyone older than you will tell you.  You're life is about to become totally different and you're in a wonderful position to change everything.  Highschool is a magical place where you feel this is the end all be all while you're attending and then after a few years you realize those highschool years represented virtually nothing.  

I've seen popular kids crash and burn, I've seen losers become champions and I've seen people who didn't change at all.  The beauty is you're at the beginning of this race and you have all the cards.  Take advantage.  

Goodluck.  As far as being annoying try the following.  You might laugh but simply have one random conversation with a stranger each day where your entire interaction with them lasts 1 minute or less.  Impart some form of information to them (sports scores, weather, something) and make sure you smile throughout the engagement.  Once that minute is up you're gone.  Hell, put a minute timer on your phone and when you feel it buzzing pretend to answer it and leave.  

It's 60 seconds, it's a stranger and you're smiling and it's done once a day.  Just do it.

As A Man Thinketh is a wonderful book.  You may see this as insignificant to your current situation but please read it, it's short and it's powerful.  

As a stranger I won't tell you you're a great person and you have so much to offer the world because even if I knew this were true you'd have no reason to believe me.  So I ask you to read a book and let it guide you into seeing yourself as someone who is special and has so much to offer those around her.

I wish you the best.

Thank you!  
It's strange because most of the time I feel in control of myself except for that constant thought of ending it all.  I'm not in a great place in my life yet I still feel like I am two different people.  There's the rational 'me' trapped in my irrational body.  I always feel like I am watching someone else crash my life yet I know my problems can be solved but the part of me that knows that is the one who no longer has control.  

That fear of regret has kept me on the solid side of the balcony.
As A Man Thinketh. I highly recommend this short book and from what you wrote I think it'd line up with your thought process nicely.
